title: Two crashes, two fixes
intro: Recipe Box's web layer ships with three planted bugs. Two of them crash, and each crash hands you a different kind of evidence — a Flask startup assertion and a runtime KeyError. Feed each one back verbatim and watch what /fix does with it.

provenance.source: the Recipe Box app ships only inside the module HTML, not as project files; the code, commands and error strings are taken from the module, terminal output is reconstructed

foot: Run it for real: build app.py from the module's lab, then python app.py

steps.title: It doesn't even boot
narrative: Paste the module's app.py into your recipe-box folder and run it. You never reach the server — Flask raises during registration, before the first request exists.

Read the assertion literally: View function mapping is overwriting an existing endpoint function: get_recipes. Flask is not complaining about the path. It is complaining that a second view function is claiming a rule already owned by get_recipes, because both decorators say methods=["GET"] on /recipes.
This is the friendliest bug class there is: it fails at import time, deterministically, with the offending name in the message. Most bugs are not this generous.

  File "flask/scaffold.py", line 452, in decorator

AssertionError: View function mapping is overwriting an existing endpoint function: get_recipes

state.label: Flask's URL map at import time

cells: the endpoint you meant to write does not exist

steps.title: /fix with the error pasted verbatim
narrative: Select the whole file, open chat, and paste the assertion as-is after /fix. You are not describing the problem — you are handing over the exact string Flask produced, which contains the endpoint name, the failure mode and the phase it happened in.
Gemini reads the selection, finds the two identical route rules and changes the second to methods=["POST"]. Apply it and the server starts on port 5001.
steps.youDo: Select all of app.py, then in chat: /fix AssertionError: View function mapping is overwriting an existing endpoint function: get_recipes
steps.claudeSays: It changes one list literal. It does not rename the function, reorder the routes, or refactor anything else — a narrow fix for a narrow diagnosis.

terminal.text: /fix AssertionError: View function mapping is overwriting an existing endpoint function: get_recipes

Both routes declare methods=["GET"] on "/recipes". Flask keys the URL map
by rule + method, so the second decorator tries to overwrite the first.
create_recipe should serve POST.

* Serving Flask app 'app'
 * Debug mode: on
 * Running on http://127.0.0.1:5001
Press CTRL+C to quit

steps.title: It boots, then it 500s
narrative: With the server up, send a POST that a real client would eventually send: a body missing two of the three fields. The handler indexes data["ingredients"] straight away, and a missing key in Python is not a validation error — it is a KeyError, which Flask turns into a 500.

A 500 here is a lie about whose fault it is. The client sent a bad request and got told the server broke. That distinction is the whole difference between 4xx and 5xx, and it is what your on-call rotation pages on.

steps.title: /fix with a described requirement
narrative: This time there is no error string worth pasting — a KeyError tells you which key was absent, not what should happen instead. So the evidence you supply is a requirement: what it does now, and what it should do, including the status code and the content of the message.

Gemini returns a handler that calls request.get_json(silent=True) so a malformed body is None rather than another exception, collects the missing keys into a list, and returns a 400 naming them. Re-run the same curl: a clean 400, and the server log stays traceback-free.

One bug is still live and it never crashes. The successful creation path returns 200 where REST convention is 201 Created — that one you find with /explain used as a convention checker, not with /fix, because nothing has gone wrong enough to complain.
steps.youDo: Select create_recipe, then: /fix this returns a 500 KeyError when fields are missing. It should validate the JSON body and return a 400 with a helpful message listing missing fields.

terminal.text:
/fix this returns a 500 KeyError when fields are missing. It should validate
the JSON body and return a 400 with a helpful message listing missing fields.

Validating before indexing. get_json(silent=True) avoids a second exception
class for malformed JSON, and the missing-field list is built in one pass so
the client learns everything that's wrong in one round trip.
/explain what HTTP status code should a successful resource creation return, and is this code following that convention?

REST convention for a successful creation is 201 Created, not 200 OK.
Your return is `jsonify({"id": new_id}), 200`. Third bug found — and
nothing had to crash for it to surface.
